rule: Visual needs the wording rules in build_visual_requirements.py cannot see, each with its reason. The first seven were added by Codex on 2026-10-18 and reviewed here (kept: each reason holds). The rest come from Claude's review the same day, against the syllabus and the 2020-2025 papers. Objectives are named by opening words so that renumbering cannot move them.

additions.objective_starts: calculate the magnification and size of biological specimens
additions.reason: Codex: magnification and size are calculated from an image with a measurable feature or scale bar

additions.objective_starts: describe the effects of osmosis on plant tissues
additions.reason: Codex: turgid, flaccid and plasmolysed cells are recognised in micrographs

additions.objective_starts: describe the effects of osmosis on animal tissues
additions.reason: Codex: red cells swollen, normal and shrivelled

additions.objective_starts: investigate and explain the effects of immersing plant tissues
additions.reason: Codex: plasmolysis seen under the microscope

additions.objective_starts: design and carry out experiments to investigate osmosis
additions.reason: Codex: epidermis under the microscope; results graphed

additions.objective_starts: identify and describe the structure of a dicotyledonous root
additions.reason: Codex: the source bullet says from photomicrographs and as seen under the light microscope; splitting dropped it

additions.objective_starts: identify and describe the structure of a dicotyledonous stem
additions.reason: Codex: as for the root

additions.objective_starts: calculate the magnification of a drawing of a specimen
additions.reason: the source bullet says from an image of a specimen; splitting dropped it (2023 P3 2(c): magnification from a measured line on a figure)

additions.objective_starts: construct and use simple dichotomous keys
additions.reason: keys are set on pictured organisms or traces (2025 P2 1(a) footprints; 2022 P2 1(a) fish)

additions.objective_starts: list the visible external features used to classify
additions.reason: visible external features are learned and tested on pictured organisms, including unfamiliar ones (2024 P2 1(b) insect features)

additions.objective_starts: describe the structural adaptations and functions of the parts of insect-pollinated
additions.reason: recognising an unfamiliar flower as insect-pollinated needs a photograph

additions.objective_starts: describe the structural adaptations and functions of the parts of wind-pollinated
additions.reason: as for insect-pollinated flowers

additions.objective_starts: describe the adaptive features of hydrophytes
additions.reason: adaptive features are read from photographs of real plants

additions.objective_starts: describe the adaptive features of xerophytes
additions.reason: adaptive features of local xerophytes (quiver tree, aloe) are read from photographs

additions.objective_starts: make temporary mounts of the upper and lower epidermis
additions.reason: the result is an epidermal peel showing stomata

additions.objective_starts: investigate and compare the relative number of stomata
additions.reason: stomata are counted on epidermal micrographs

additions.objective_starts: explain the effect of changes in temperature on enzyme activity
additions.reason: the rate-temperature curve, with its optimum, is the standard representation

additions.objective_starts: explain the effect of changes in pH on enzyme activity
additions.reason: the rate-pH curve

additions.objective_starts: describe the effect of varying light intensity on the rate of photosynthesis
additions.reason: rate against light intensity, levelling off where another factor limits

additions.objective_starts: describe the effect of varying carbon dioxide concentration on the rate of photosynthesis
additions.reason: rate against carbon dioxide concentration

additions.objective_starts: identify and explain the limiting factors of photosynthesis
additions.reason: limiting factors are identified from the plateau of a rate graph

additions.objective_starts: explain the effects of physical activity on the rate and depth of breathing
additions.reason: read from a graph in the papers (2024 P2 4(b)(ii))

additions.objective_starts: explain accommodation to view distant objects
additions.reason: Claude, 2026-10-18: sibling of the near-object objective, which already needs a diagram; ciliary muscle, suspensory ligament and lens shape are explained from a diagram of the eye in both cases

additions.objective_starts: explain the pupil reflex
additions.reason: Claude, 2026-10-18: the antagonistic circular and radial muscles of the iris are taught from a front-view diagram in bright and dim light
